candidates.source_name: ČNB – Centrální úložiště regulovaných informací (OAM / Central Storage of Regulated Information), CZ interface
candidates.why_relevant: This is the officially appointed mechanism (OAM) under Directive 2004/109/EC where every issuer of securities admitted to a Czech regulated market files regulated information. It holds the actual documents (výroční zpráva / annual financial report, pololetní zpráva / half-yearly report, vnitřní informace / inside information, manažerské transakce, oznámení o podílu na hlasovacích právech, zprávy o platbách vládám, nefinanční informace). Its issuer dropdown simultaneously acts as a definitive pointer: it enumerates every issuer with securities on a regulated market (RT) or MTF (MOS/OOS), which is the master list of Czech bank and payments issuers whose IR/disclosure sites must exist.
candidates.legal_status: official public register operated by a public authority; re-use likely permitted but ČNB site terms not read in this run
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scripted form-driven crawl of the Oracle PL/SQL web app: enumerate the issuer dropdown to build the issuer master list, then iterate the date-range + information-type filters to harvest filing metadata and linked documents. Session/cookie handling required; deep links appear parameterised via p_lang and filter POSTs. Schedule daily; snapshot the issuer dropdown separately as an entity index.
candidates.discovered_via_method: cs-language seed query + snowball from ČNB supervision navigation
queries_used: ČNB centrální úložiště regulovaných informací emitenti archiv

candidates.source_name: ČNB – JERRS, Seznamy regulovaných a registrovaných subjektů finančního trhu
candidates.why_relevant: THE authoritative index of who exists in the Czech financial market: every entity that received a licence/authorisation, was registered, notified or entered into a ČNB-maintained list — banks and branches of foreign banks, credit unions, payment institutions, e-money institutions, small-scale payment service providers and small-scale e-money issuers, securities dealers, insurers. Provides exact wording of the authorisation, activity type, IČO, date of issue and current status (valid / suspended / revoked). Because every licensed entity has statutory disclosure duties, this register is the generator of the target list of disclosure/IR sites for the whole workstream. Also exposes counts by date and time series of entity creation/termination (market-structure signal).
candidates.legal_status: official public register; ČNB is legally obliged to publish these lists

candidates.source_name: ČNB – WS JERRS web services (SOAP API to the register of regulated entities)
candidates.why_relevant: Machine-readable access to JERRS, live since 1 July 2019. Three operations: subject information (identification, seat, authorisation dates, permitted activities, relationships), subject list by role category (paginated), and representatives of a represented entity (paginated). This is the cleanest way to maintain a continuously refreshed entity master list without scraping. Endpoint observed as https://aplc.cnb.cz/jerrsws/ws with JerrsWS.wsdl / JerrsWS.xsd; XML request/response.
candidates.legal_status: official ČNB service; access granted on written, electronically signed request

Treat as the primary entity feed once provisioned; scrape JERRS HTML only as fallback.

candidates.why_relevant: Register of prospectuses approved by ČNB and prospectuses notified into CZ from other member states, under Regulation (EU) 2017/1129. candidates.why_relevant: Explains the filing regime that produces OAM content: which reports are due (pololetní zpráva, výroční finanční zpráva, oznámení o změně podílu na hlasovacích právech, manažerské transakce, oznámení o odkladu uveřejnění vnitřní informace), the legal basis (vyhláška č. 234/2009 Sb.; Regulations 236/2012 and 596/2014) and that filings go through SDAT. candidates.source_name: ESMA – Prospectus Register and the European Single Access Point (ESAP)
candidates.why_relevant: ESMA's prospectus register aggregates approved prospectuses, related documents and issuer/security metadata across NCAs including ČNB, giving a second route to CZ bank bond prospectuses with harmonised metadata. ESAP (Regulation (EU) 2023/2859) will, from 2026-2027, ingest from collection bodies — the national OAMs, i.e. the ČNB Central Storage — via a standardised API and expose it centrally, which will eventually make CZ regulated information retrievable without scraping the ČNB Oracle apps. Track now as a forward-looking infrastructure change.

Set a standing watch on ESAP milestones (collection-body onboarding in 2026, public access targeted 2027) and plan a migration of the OAM collector to the ESAP API when it opens.

candidates.source_name: Veřejný rejstřík a Sbírka listin (or.justice.cz) — statutory filing archive
candidates.why_relevant: The natural downstream of the ČNB registers: every entity found in JERRS carries an IČO, and that IČO resolves in the sbírka listin to its účetní závěrka and výroční zpráva as free PDFs. This is the only route to full annual-report coverage for the large majority of CZ banks, payment institutions and small-scale PSPs that are NOT listed issuers and therefore never appear in OAM. Statutory deadlines (filing within 30 days of approval, at the latest 12 months after the balance-sheet date) give a predictable collection calendar.
candidates.legal_status: public register maintained by the registry courts; documents are public by law
candidates.suggested_collection_method: IČO-driven crawl seeded from the ČNB open-data CSVs and JERRS: for each IČO, enumerate sbírka listin entries and download výroční zpráva / účetní závěrka PDFs. Rate-limit politely; run annually with a rolling monthly sweep during the March-July filing season.

Complements the ČNB registers: OAM covers regulated-market issuers, but START/Free market issuers have exchange-level rather than statutory disclosure duties, so PSE is the only index of that population. Also useful for confirming ISINs and listing status when reconciling the OAM issuer dropdown.
candidates.legal_status: commercial market operator; site terms not reviewed in this run
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl the issuer/market listing pages per market segment to build a listed-issuer roster with ISINs; fetch Burzovní pravidla PDFs once for the disclosure-duty model. Reconcile against the OAM issuer dropdown to find issuers present in one and not the other.
candidates.discovered_via_method: cs snowball from the issuer disclosure-obligations theme
queries_used: Burza cenných papírů Praha emitenti informační povinnost zveřejňování pse.cz

negative_findings.description: ČNB's Otevřená data page exposes exactly seven datasets (banks and branches of foreign banks, exchange offices, non-bank consumer credit providers, independent credit intermediaries, tied credit representatives, tied credit intermediaries, foreign credit intermediaries). There is NO open dataset for platební instituce, instituce elektronických peněz, poskytovatelé platebních služeb malého rozsahu or vydavatelé elektronických peněz malého rozsahu.
negative_findings.result_summary: Bulk CSV/JSON access covers the banking and credit-intermediation side only; the payments population must be obtained by scraping JERRS, by using WS JERRS with a certificate, from the ČNB PSRI statistical list, or from the EBA PSD2 register.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The payments half of the sector — the fastest-changing population and the one most relevant to a payments market-intelligence programme — has no frictionless machine-readable feed from the national regulator. Collection design must not assume symmetry with the banking datasets.

negative_findings.description: WS JERRS, the only official API over the register of regulated entities, requires a commercial certificate from an approved CA and an electronically signed access request emailed to jerrsws@cnb.cz before any call can be made.
negative_findings.result_summary: No anonymous or key-based access exists; provisioning is a manual, paperwork-bound process with an unknown lead time.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cleanest entity feed cannot be switched on in a research sprint. Either budget for the certificate and application process up front, or design the pipeline around HTML scraping plus the seven open-data CSVs from day one.

negative_findings.description: A guessed JERRS deep link (https://jerrs.cnb.cz/apljerrsdad/JERRS.WEB10.HLEDANI_SUBJEKTU?p_lang=cz) returned HTTP 500. The ČNB applications are Oracle PL/SQL web apps whose procedure names and parameters are not documented publicly.
negative_findings.result_summary: Hypothesis, not a verdict: the entry points that were actually observed (JERRS.WEB07.INTRO_PAGE, JERRS.WEB45.LOGIN_A, SIPRESWEB.WEB21/WEB_PROSPECTUS/WEB_SHORTSELL.START_INPUT_OAM) responded, so the apps are live; only the invented procedure name failed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collectors must navigate from the ČNB short-links (/cnb/jerrs, /cnb/registr_prospektu, /cnb/kratke_pozice_cz) and follow redirects and forms rather than hard-coding internal procedure URLs, which will break or 500 without notice.

negative_findings.description: Several fetches of www.cnb.cz returned ECONNRESET, 'socket hang up', or a domain-safety block from the fetching layer, while the same or adjacent URLs succeeded on retry.
negative_findings.result_summary: Treated as transient network/bot-defence behaviour, NOT as evidence that any ČNB URL is dead. All ČNB URLs recorded here are unverified for liveness by design and must be confirmed by the deterministic verification pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A naive liveness checker will mark ČNB pages dead on first failure and prune the single most important source cluster in the whole CZ landscape. Retries with backoff and a realistic user agent are required.

negative_findings.description: For the ČNB Registr prospektů it could not be confirmed from the register's own page whether the full prospectus PDFs are hosted and downloadable from ČNB, or whether the register carries only metadata plus a reference to the issuer's own publication. ČNB explicitly states that publication in the list does not replace the issuer's publication duty under Regulation (EU) 2017/1129.
negative_findings.result_summary: Open question requiring a hands-on retrieval test against a known Czech bank base prospectus.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Determines whether the prospectus collector is a document harvester or only a metadata index that must then be joined to issuer websites — a materially different build.

negative_findings.description: The European Single Access Point, which is intended to aggregate national OAM content including the ČNB Central Storage, is not yet a usable source: collection from collection bodies is scheduled to begin around July 2026 with public access targeted for July 2027 under Regulation (EU) 2023/2859.
negative_findings.result_summary: ESAP cannot be used as a substitute for scraping the ČNB OAM in the current run; it is a watch item, not a source.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Avoids designing the CZ disclosure collector around an access point that will not deliver data in this planning horizon, while flagging a foreseeable migration that will reduce scraping cost later.

negative_findings.description: Two local-language pitfalls were observed. First, the bare phrase 'seznam ČNB' is heavily reused by commercial finance portals (finanza.cz, penize.cz and similar) that republish ČNB register extracts, so it retrieves mirrors rather than the primary source. Second, 'OAM' is not Czech usage — it is the EU 'officially appointed mechanism' concept surviving only in the oam.cnb.cz hostname; the Czech public name is 'centrální úložiště regulovaných informací'.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches must use the full Czech official names; the acronym OAM is useful only for URL pattern matching, not for Czech-language retrieval.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Query design that relies on acronyms or short forms will surface secondary aggregators and mis-attribute authority, contaminating a source register meant to record primary sources.

negative_findings.description: No robots.txt, terms-of-use or re-use licence was read for www.cnb.cz, oam.cnb.cz, jerrs.cnb.cz, or.justice.cz or pse.cz during this run.
negative_findings.result_summary: Legal status recorded for each candidate is inferred from the public-register character of the sources and, for the ČNB open data, from the explicit open-data regime under nařízení vlády č. 425/2016 Sb. — not from a read licence document, except where stated.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Automated collection at scale should be gated on an explicit robots/ToS check per host before the collectors go into production, particularly for or.justice.cz and pse.cz which are not open-data publishers.

coverage_gaps.description: The ČNB Central Storage (OAM) offers no documented API, RSS feed or bulk export; it is a form-driven Oracle web application. Every regulated filing must be reached through session-bound queries.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a resilient session-aware crawler with issuer-dropdown enumeration and date-window paging, plus checkpointing. In parallel, ask ČNB directly (the site publishes a §106 information-request channel) whether a machine-readable export or feed of OAM content exists, and set a watch on ESAP onboarding as the eventual replacement.

coverage_gaps.description: This cell established WHERE the CZ payment institution / EMI / small-scale PSP registers live (JERRS, PSRI list, EBA PSD2 register) but did not extract the actual entity roster or counts, and did not confirm which JERRS role codes correspond to each of the four Czech payments licence categories.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated extraction pass that enumerates JERRS role categories, records the exact Czech role labels and their identifiers, and produces a reconciled CZ payments entity list joined against the ČNB PSRI list and the EBA register.

coverage_gaps.description: JERRS presents current status (valid / suspended / revoked) and offers aggregate counts and creation/termination time series, but it is unclear whether per-entity historical states (previous names, past authorisation scopes, withdrawal dates) are retrievable retrospectively.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Start snapshotting the open-data CSVs and JERRS category listings weekly from day one to build an internal point-in-time history, rather than assuming ČNB can reconstruct it later. Test whether WS JERRS returns authorisation date ranges and prior states.

coverage_gaps.description: English interfaces exist for OAM (/cnb/oam_en), JERRS (/cnb/jerrs_en) and the ČNB lists hub, but whether the English content and lists are updated in step with the Czech originals was not tested.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Collect the Czech versions as the authoritative record and use the English versions only for label mapping; run a one-off content-parity check on a sample of entities and filings before relying on any EN page as a data source.

coverage_gaps.description: Branches of foreign banks and passported EEA payment institutions operating in CZ typically disclose in their home member state's OAM rather than in the ČNB storage, and this cell did not map which CZ-active entities fall into that category or where their filings actually land.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Use the ČNB 'banky a pobočky zahraničních bank' open dataset and the EBA registers to segment CZ-active entities into domestic filers versus home-state filers, then record the corresponding foreign OAMs as separate sources in a later pass.

coverage_gaps.description: Registers of pověření zástupci (payment service agents), vázaní zástupci and samostatní zprostředkovatelé — fed through REGIS and surfaced in JERRS and the open data — were identified but not enumerated. These reveal distribution networks and white-label payment arrangements that are otherwise invisible.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a dedicated extraction of the agent/representative lists (including the WS JERRS representatives operation and the EBA agent data) as a follow-on task; they are high-volume and need their own change-detection cadence.

coverage_gaps.description: The date coverage of the ČNB prospectus register and of the final-terms register was not established — in particular whether records predating Regulation (EU) 2017/1129 (i.e. pre-July 2019 approvals under the old prospectus directive regime) remain searchable.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Probe both registers with wide historical date ranges and a known older Czech bank bond programme to establish the earliest retrievable record, and document the cut-off in the source register.

brief: For Czech banking and payments, the Czech National Bank is not one source but a small federation of disclosure infrastructure, and it is the correct starting index for the entire landscape. Three OAM-family applications on oam.cnb.cz carry the filed content — the centrální úložiště regulovaných informací (annual and half-yearly reports, inside information, managers' transactions, major-holdings notifications, plus a pre-2009 archive), the registr prospektů and the registr konečných podmínek základních prospektů, and the short-positions register — while JERRS on jerrs.cnb.cz is the authoritative roster of every licensed bank, payment institution, e-money institution and small-scale payment service provider, exposed as HTML, as seven open-data CSV/JSON datasets, and as a certificate-gated SOAP API (WS JERRS). The decisive asymmetry for this run is that the frictionless bulk feeds cover the banking and credit-intermediation side only: the payments categories have no open dataset and must be reached by scraping JERRS, by the ČNB PSRI statistical list, or via the EBA PSD2 register, and the OAM itself has no export at all until ESAP arrives in 2027. Because most CZ banks and payment institutions are not listed issuers and never appear in OAM, the IČO exposed by every ČNB register is the load-bearing join key into the sbírka listin at or.justice.cz, which is where their annual reports actually live.
